policy_note: Registry entries are convenience hints, not permanent approvals. Every incorporation must still verify the exact commit/tag/package version and exact file/path license scope.

statuses.PASS: May incorporate only after exact-scope verification and notice recording.
statuses.CONDITIONAL: Only explicitly permissive paths may be incorporated; restricted paths are blocked.
statuses.STUDY_ONLY: May study public product behavior/docs/architecture concepts; do not copy implementation source.
statuses.BLOCKED: Do not incorporate without explicit legal/commercial-license review.

repositories.name: Supabase
allowed_scope: files proven covered by Apache-2.0 at the pinned ref
excluded_scope: third-party assets or components with separate terms unless independently verified
repositories.notes: Preserve applicable LICENSE and NOTICE obligations.

repositories.name: Tiptap core

repositories.name: FullCalendar Standard
repositories.license: MIT for Standard packages; Premium has separate licensing
allowed_scope: Standard packages/files explicitly covered by MIT at the pinned ref
excluded_scope: Premium/Scheduler/resource premium packages unless a compatible commercial license is verified
repositories.notes: Do not infer Premium permission from the Standard MIT license. Re-verified 2026-08-12 at v7.0.2: @fullcalendar/core and @fullcalendar/react npm metadata are MIT (daygrid/timegrid/list/multimonth/interaction are subpath exports of the react package); Premium packages (e.g. @fullcalendar/premium-common@6.1.21) carry 'SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md' custom commercial terms and are published from the separate fullcalendar-workspace repo; @fullcalendar/scheduler no longer exists on npm.

repositories.name: Cal.diy

repositories.name: Cal.com production/private codebase
repositories.license: Private/proprietary production codebase as of April 2026

excluded_scope: private production source, leaked/mirrored source, enterprise/commercial source without a verified license
repositories.notes: Do not use old mirrors or historical public source to bypass current licensing. Historical AGPL/open-core code requires separate review if deliberately used.
